evidence: Plaut. Curc. 132: ecce autem bibit arcus, pluet crēdō hercle hodiē
terms.comment: The plain future, as Plautus’s slave says it when he sees a rainbow, often with crēdō. Traupman’s Vidētur quasi pluat says “it looks as if it’s raining”; the future says what is coming.

terms.gloss: rain is threatening, rain is on the way
terms.grammar: impendeō, intransitive; of any weather: tempestās impendet
evidence: Verg. G. 4.191: nec vērō ā stabulīs pluviā impendente recēdunt longius

phrases.latin: ecce autem bibit arcus, pluet crēdō hercle hodiē
phrases.english: look, the rainbow’s drinking; it’ll rain today, I bet

phrases.latin: nec vērō ā stabulīs pluviā impendente recēdunt longius
phrases.english: and when rain is coming they do not go far from their hives
It’s going to rain, I think; put your coat on.

sources: Lewis & Short: pluo · Lewis & Short: impendeo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 136.
